record.original_question: The quotient criterion says, in regular and chiral settings, that under suitable facet hypotheses a regular cover is again polytopal. Find a combinatorial criterion, usable for arbitrary polytopes or maniplexes rather than only regular or chiral ones, that plays the role of this quotient criterion.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Find a combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. An abstract n-polytope is a ranked partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) have ranks in {-1,0,...,n} with unique minimum and maximum, in which every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly one face of each rank, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever F < G with rank(G) = rank(F)+2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G. The facets are the faces of rank n-1. A maniplex of rank n is an edge-n-colored connected graph in which, for each pair of distinct colors i,j with |i-j| > 1, every connected component of the subgraph spanned by edges of colors i and j is a 4-cycle; abstract polytopes correspond to maniplexes satisfying the (strong) path-intersection property. A polytope (or maniplex) Q is a cover of P if there is a rank- and adjacency-preserving surjection of flags from Q to P. A polytope is called regular if its automorphism group acts transitively on flags, and chiral if it has two orbits of flags under automorphisms with adjacent flags lying in different orbits.

A known "quotient criterion" in the regular and chiral settings states that, under suitable assumptions on the facets, a regular (respectively chiral) cover of a regular (respectively chiral) polytope is itself polytopal, i.e. satisfies the intersection property. 

Problem. Formulate and prove a purely combinatorial criterion, applicable to arbitrary abstract polytopes or maniplexes (not assumed to be regular or chiral), which serves the same role as the quotient criterion: namely, given a cover Q -> P of polytopes (or maniplexes), provide combinatorial conditions under which the polytopality (intersection property) of P, together with hypotheses on the facets, guarantees polytopality of Q.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a paper providing a general combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion for arbitrary polytopes or maniplexes. Related work on symmetry type graphs and k-orbit polytopes/maniplexes exists, but none of the results found directly resolves the problem as stated.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry Type Graphs of Polytopes and Maniplexes
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces symmetry type graphs and discusses k-orbit maniplexes/polytopes; does not state a general quotient criterion analogue.
status_evidence.claim: No general combinatorial analogue of the quotient criterion is provided here.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes via coset geometries.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses k-orbit polytopes but does not give a general quotient criterion for arbitrary covers.
